artworks.title: Sthenelos bandaging the wounded finger of Diomedes
artworks.description: Wellcome ink drawing after a Chalcidian neck-amphora: Sthenelus binds Diomedes' wounded finger — Capaneus' son as the comrade who tends the Argive champion in the Iliad's orbit.

artworks.title: Sthenelos and Diomedes
artworks.description: Nineteenth-century Baumeister plate of Sthenelus with Diomedes — the Epigone and chariot-mate whose Iliadic vaunt answers Agamemnon with Capaneus' son's pride.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Book IV — Sthenelus answers Agamemnon beside Diomedes: we took Thebes when our fathers failed. Capaneus' son as the Epigone who still rides at Troy.

popCulture.title: Epigoni
popCulture.description: The sons who avenged the Seven — Sthenelus marches among them before he becomes Diomedes' steadfast companion at Troy.

popCulture.title: Sthenelus (son of Capaneus)
popCulture.description: Son of Capaneus, Epigone and Iliadic comrade of Diomedes — distinct from Sthenelus the Perseid father of Eurystheus.
